Could Indonesia’s proposed MSCI reclassification benefit Malaysia?

MSCI is consulting on whether to move Indonesia from Emerging Market to Standalone Market status, with a final decision expected by the end of June 2027.

If the move goes ahead, Malaysia’s weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index would rise slightly, all else being equal. Funds that track the index would rebalance, potentially lifting foreign demand for Malaysian stocks already in the benchmark.

The immediate benefit would likely be modest. Indonesia accounted for around 0.4% of the index in early November 2026, and its weight would be redistributed across all remaining markets. Active investors could also react differently, especially if they see the decision as a reason to reduce exposure to Southeast Asia as a whole.

My takeaway for Malaysia is that index changes can bring some buying, but keeping international investors comes down to fundamentals we can influence: transparent ownership, strong corporate governance and enough market liquidity for investors to trade efficiently.

What would make Bursa Malaysia more attractive to long-term global investors?

This was my first EuroCham Indonesia (The European Business Chamber of Commerce in Indonesia) gathering to participate in and it was more interesting and informative than the mainstream headlines in the news we read.
 
This last Tuesday theEuroCham Indonesia (The European Business Chamber of Commerce in Indonesia) held the Energy Dinner 2026 at Rumah Imam Bonjol in Menteng, Jakarta. I was happy to participate as I was finally able to meet PakEdison Bako in person along with several European businesses and Indonesian government officials to talk about Indonesia's energy future and what is being seen on the ground. 
 
The Guest of Honor, Deputy Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Bpk Dradjad Hari Wibowo, kept his message simple and candidly explained that energy transition cooperation needs to move beyond commitments and targets, toward bankable projects, real investment, and measurable results.
 
He asked EuroCham’s Energy Working Group and its members to take 3 practical steps:
 
1. Prioritize high-potential projects in#renewables, #biofuels, #hydrogen, and waste-to-energy (#WtE)
2. Build stronger links between European investors and technology providers, the state power company PT PLN (Persero), Indonesia’s sovereign investment fund Danantara Indonesia , developers, and industrial users
3. Move faster, with clear project ownership and a 90-day action plan
 
I fully understand that nobody’s saying things are perfect and there are real problems to work through. But from the conversations and what we heard, things are more promising than much of what we read in the news.
 
Pictured with PakEdison Bako, Executive Director of EuroCham Indonesia. Thank you to EuroCham Indonesia (The European Business Chamber of Commerce in Indonesia), and the Energy Working Group for a great evening.

Anthropic wants an architect in Paris. French required

Google wants engineers who build AI agents inside customer companies in Mexico and Argentina. Spanish required.

Google also wants customer engineers who speak Polish, and Bahasa Indonesia.

The job is the same each time: sit with the customer, connect AI to the systems they already use, and test it on their own cases.

Google's ad names the real blockers plainly: "integration complexities" and "data readiness". Not the model.

None of these roles are in the Gulf or Turkey. The work is the same here, and it needs Arabic, Turkish, and people who know your ERP, CRM and WhatsApp.

Before you pick a partner for an AI agent, ask three things:
Will they work with your team in your language?
Will they connect to the systems you already use, or ask you to move to new ones?

Will they test the agent on your own past cases before it goes live?

This was my first EuroCham Indonesia (The European Business Chamber of Commerce in Indonesia) gathering to participate in and it was more interesting and informative than the mainstream headlines in the news we read.
 
This last Tuesday theEuroCham Indonesia (The European Business Chamber of Commerce in Indonesia) held the Energy Dinner 2026 at Rumah Imam Bonjol in Menteng, Jakarta. I was happy to participate as I was finally able to meet PakEdison Bako in person along with several European businesses and Indonesian government officials to talk about Indonesia's energy future and what is being seen on the ground. 
 
The Guest of Honor, Deputy Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Bpk Dradjad Hari Wibowo, kept his message simple and candidly explained that energy transition cooperation needs to move beyond commitments and targets, toward bankable projects, real investment, and measurable results.
 
He asked EuroCham’s Energy Working Group and its members to take 3 practical steps:
 
1. Prioritize high-potential projects in#renewables, #biofuels, #hydrogen, and waste-to-energy (#WtE)
2. Build stronger links between European investors and technology providers, the state power company PT PLN (Persero), Indonesia’s sovereign investment fund Danantara Indonesia , developers, and industrial users
3. Move faster, with clear project ownership and a 90-day action plan
 
I fully understand that nobody’s saying things are perfect and there are real problems to work through. But from the conversations and what we heard, things are more promising than much of what we read in the news.
 
Pictured with PakEdison Bako, Executive Director of EuroCham Indonesia. Thank you to EuroCham Indonesia (The European Business Chamber of Commerce in Indonesia), and the Energy Working Group for a great evening.
